fix(client): clarify mobile native-open feedback (#6660)

* feat(ui-open-in-app): announce settled open outcomes app-wide

The shared file and directory opener reported a nullable failure, so it could
not tell a handoff the Host acknowledged from a gesture an adapter deliberately
dropped — a duplicate already in flight, or a controller disposed before the
gesture ran. Its notice also lived inside the control that asked for the open,
so it died with the panel, tab, or card the gesture started in.

Replace that with a discriminated outcome on both controllers and adapters, and
report each settled gesture into one `shell.overlay` entry that renders the
app-wide Toast: the Session-header command, the files-tab and Session-header
buttons, both document-preview controls, and both delivery-card controls.
`{ kind: 'skipped' }` announces nothing, because no handoff happened, so card
status and the toast never disagree about what settled.

Name the action for what it does on every surface — "Open on your computer" —
instead of after whichever application would take the handoff. The application
stays supplementary, in the tooltip beside the shortcut it runs under, which is
what the accessible name, visible text, and command label now share.

* fix(client): unify open-in-app feedback

* fix(client): report native open outcomes accurately

* test(ptc): synchronize hot-loop log capture

Observe a synchronous child marker before cancellation so the console retention assertion does not depend on completing Node startup within one second.

* fix(client): scope native-open feedback to mobile

Explain native opens on another device for mobile and PWA clients while keeping desktop success silent. Preserve failure feedback after the initiating surface closes and ignore skipped requests.

fix(chat): keep the transcript steady at Turn end and when steering lands

Measured against 0.2.1-rc.4 and master with the frame-sampled motion matrix,
the transcript moved back and forth at Turn end and around input landing.
This keeps rc.4's landing behavior, master's steering layout, and fixes the
reversals that remain.

- Completion-time folding keeps the first visible surviving row still when
  work rows close at once, filling the gap with bottom space capped at half
  the scrollport, instead of letting the browser clamp the position.
- After the Session stops running, the running status keeps its tail slot
  hidden and silent until the Turn's actions row replaces it, so the tail
  does not shrink and grow back.
- A Turn's duration control takes its gap in one frame instead of sliding.
- A fold batch that takes over following for a content change absorbs
  growth outside the batch before its first frame.
- Steering lands at once under either fold timing: the running Turn keeps
  streaming above its echo, which a native animation would push down.
- The running status no longer slides below a Step's first output, and the
  column no longer carries `data-chat-tail-pinned`; the steering entrance
  keeps its animation.
- A queued prompt is accepted by its Inbox row as well as by its receipt,
  so the composer clears the draft in the frame the queue dock shows it.
- A queued echo waits for the Inbox projection instead of retiring on the
  durable splice, so the queue dock does not empty for a frame.

fix(session-controller): retire a queued echo when its Inbox row is canceled

A queued echo now records its Inbox position like transcript and steering
echoes. Later splices move that position, so a canceled splice that removes
the row retires the echo even when no Inbox projection ever showed it, for
example when the Turn is stopped right after queueing. A claimed row still
waits for its admitted message, and the queue dock still hands the echo over
to the Host row it renders.

The fold-room e2e no longer samples the running status slide or the
`data-chat-tail-pinned` mark that this branch removed. It asserts that fold
room below a short answer takes the new Turn's growth without scrolling
through Turn end, that the room never grows back, and that the running
status only moves down.

feat(models): show model selector badges from the /models listing (#7027)

* refactor(llm-deepseek): share the /models listing machinery

Move the account route's `/models` request and decoding, its
credential-scoped listing cache, and listed-catalog resolution with the
version gate into the shared DeepSeek Messages library, so a second
route can follow the same listing. Names drop the account prefix, the
cache takes each access's endpoint settings with the call, and it gains
`invalidate()` for a forced reload. `isBuiltInCatalog()` recognizes the
catalog an uncustomized `models` setting resolves to.

The account route keeps its behavior; only its imports and the
override diagnostic wording ("model listing") change.

* feat(llm-deepseek-api-key): follow the official /models listing

While `models` equals the built-in catalog and the Messages origin is
https://api.deepseek.com, `deepseek-official` serves the official
`GET /models` listing, authenticated with the API key in `x-api-key`.
Loading, refresh, fallback, merging, and the client-version gate match
the account route: the first access waits up to `modelsTimeoutMs`, a
listing older than `modelsMaxAgeMs` refreshes in the background on the
next access, a failure keeps the last good listing or the built-in
catalog, and listed models this build cannot serve are refused before
network I/O.

A customized `models` list replaces the catalog and requests nothing.
Switching between a customized catalog and the listing discards the
cached listing, so Restore defaults reloads it on the next access.

Suites that boot the route on the official endpoint now answer the
listing themselves instead of reaching the network.

* docs: describe the official route model listing

Document when `deepseek-official` follows the official `/models`
listing, its timing fields, customization precedence, and the forced
reload after Restore defaults in the API-key README, the shared
transport README, and the provider guide. Record the decision in a new
Agent Note, keep the account note's statement of where the shared
listing code lives current, and regenerate the configuration catalog.

* test(llm-deepseek-api-key): pin the once-per-listing hidden-entry diagnostic

* docs: regenerate module and event graphs for the shared listing

* fix(llm-deepseek-api-key): report credential failures on the model request

On the official endpoint, `connect` waited for the listing view, whose
credential lookup rethrew a malformed key or a credential-store failure
before the agent loop recorded the prompt. A failed lookup now resolves
the connection from the current listing view, so `resolveAuth` reports
the failure on the model request and the turn keeps the prompt and the
failed attempt. A caller abort still rejects.

* docs(llm-deepseek-api-key): name which hidden listing entries are logged

* test: keep unit suites off the official model listing

Suites that boot the DeepSeek routes with a dummy or inherited key now
request `GET https://api.deepseek.com/models` on the official endpoint.
A unit-lane setup file rejects that request at once, so such a suite
serves the built-in catalog instead of reaching production or waiting
out the listing deadline on a network that never answers; suites that
exercise the listing answer `fetch` themselves. Other requests pass
through unchanged.

* feat(llm-deepseek): read tool_update from the model listing

Both DeepSeek routes now take a listed model's Messages tool update mode
from `api_capabilities.anthropic_messages.tool_update`, alongside the
system prompt mode. `in-history` and `addition-only` replace the
bundled mode; any other value reads as `leading-only` and removes it.
An absent or `null` mode keeps the bundled one, so a listing that does
not declare the field leaves `deepseek-flash` on `addition-only`.

`system_prompt_update: null` likewise keeps the bundled mode now; it
previously read as `leading-only`, which a serializer writing empty
values as null would have turned into a cache-unfriendly downgrade.

* fix(llm-deepseek): sync the built-in context window with the official listing

The official `/models` listing declares a 1,048,576-token context window
for `deepseek-flash` and `deepseek-v4-pro`; the built-in catalog said
1,000,000, a decimal-versus-binary mismatch. Both built-in entries now
carry the listed value, so offline starts and listing failures size the
context the same way the listing does. The Models page shows the exact
count for these rows, since 1,048,576 has no decimal K/M spelling.

`defaultContextWindow`, the fallback for model ids the catalog does not
describe, stays 1,000,000.

* test(llm-deepseek-api-key): reject the stubbed listing request with an Error

* test(cli): keep the built SDK smoke off the official model listing

The SDK profile's initialize now resolves the deepseek-official catalog,
which requests GET https://api.deepseek.com/models on the official
endpoint. With the smoke's fixture key that request answers 401 and the
route warns on stderr, so the test's empty-stderr assertion failed in the
e2e and snapshots lanes. Point the run at a loopback mock and assert it
received no model call.

* feat(llm): carry /models badges into the model catalog

The shared DeepSeek listing decoder reads an optional per-entry
`badge: { text, tone }`. Text is one literal or translations keyed by
lowercase language id with a required English entry, each trimmed to 1
to 12 characters on one line; tone is neutral, info, success, or
warning, and an absent or unrecognized tone reads as neutral. An absent
or null badge declares none; an unreadable one is dropped with a listing
problem and never hides its model.

resolveListedCatalog keeps the badges of offered models, both DeepSeek
routes attach them through catalogModelInfo, LlmRuntime.listModels
detaches them, and the Host model catalog forwards them as
ModelCatalogModel.badge. resolveModelInfo omits the badge, so no model
request, Session event, or model-facing tool carries it.

* feat(client): render catalog badges in the model selector

The composer model seat shows a catalog model's badge after its name in
the trigger, the root-menu value, and each option: a Tag in the badge's
tone whose text is resolved for the active locale through
ctx.locale.resolveText. A conversation.input.model.label contribution
replaces the name and badge together and receives the badge in its
owner props.

Remove ui-deepseek-model-label-1017, which hard-coded `1017` beside

* feat(llm-deepseek): read model badges from client_metadata

Each /models entry now declares its selector badge under
client_metadata["deepseek-harness"].badge, keyed by the User-Agent product
token like client_requirements, so the public model fields stay unchanged
and later DeepSeek Harness fields join the same object. Every field under
client_metadata is ignorable: null at any level shows no badge, and a level
that is not an object drops only the badge with a diagnostic naming it.

feat(liveshare): add the host, viewer, and client share surfaces (#6749)

* feat(liveshare): add the owner host, viewer host, and share runtime

The owner-side half of the bundle: the share host that publishes a Session to a Relay and answers one viewer per share, the owner credential/authorization records, the fork registry and its enforcement, the read-only viewer access policy and read budgets, the turn-requester fold, and the Relay gateway worker. The viewer host renders the served page's assets and declarations; no browser code is included in this layer.

* test(liveshare): cover the owner host, viewer host, and gateway

Keyless host-side coverage: share publication and restore, owner login/authority, fork registry and enforcement, viewer read policy and budgets, the turn-requester fold, the Relay tunnel worker and gateway commands, and the served viewer page. The browser surfaces are covered by the client layer's own suite.

* chore(build): register the host bundle in the compiler, dependency policy, and CI

The package manifest, Host compiler face, and tsdown host entries the bundle needs; the workspace constraints the built gateway/declaration artifacts require; the release-family and README model-experience rows; the coverage-lane exemption; and the keyless CI job that runs the share cases on Linux. The dependency-policy classifications wait for the client layer, which is where the package's client face (and its imports) first appears.

* docs(liveshare): record the bundle's subsystem, projection, and decision rationale

The package README for the host layer, the subsystem page, the persistence record that declares the viewer principal projection, and the note that keeps the protocol and owner-surface decisions with their evidence.

* feat(boot): offer the Liveshare host bundle in the CLI profile and plugin manager

The bundle joins the optional bundles the CLI installation carries and the Official group the plugin manager lists, so an owner can switch it on without editing a profile by hand. The plugin-manager and plugin-config expectations follow in the client layer that renders the card's browser half.

* chore(docs): regenerate the graphs, catalogs, and persistence records for the host

Run the generators over the host layer: the event producer/consumer graphs, the persistence catalog and schema inventory, the config catalog, the module graph, and the Cordis API catalog. The persisted viewer-principal event appears in the catalog and the historical format index counts it.

* fix(liveshare): keep the bundle's locale display metadata in this layer

The CLI profile registers the bundle as optional, so the plugin manager reads title and description from ./locale/*.json. Ship the two locale files and their export here; the browser half is not needed for display metadata.

* refactor(liveshare): read the turn boundary through the typed Agents service

The retained projection-handle migration left two assertions converted through unknown; ctx.get('agents') already exposes turnBoundaryOf, so the host and the cancel-admission case call it directly and the unknown-cast baseline stays untouched.

* test(liveshare): expect the canonical viewer tier from the three-mode harness

The Relay reports a share published with the withdrawn fork-readonly tier as view and carries the fork grant separately, so the harness compares the canonical tier and forwards an explicit allowsFork when the case names one.

* refactor(liveshare): share the reader-facing record and body readers

The fork decision and the access snapshot built the same share facts twice, and the two share-writing routes read the same share-naming JSON body twice; both pairs are now one helper each, so jscpd no longer reports them. Behavior is unchanged.

* test(web): record the host layer's optional-bundle expectations

Registering the LiveShare bundle in the Official group adds its card and description to the plugin manager and plugin-config pages, and the packed preview must state that its host plugin needs LIVESHARE_RELAY_URL instead of a generic applied toggle. Refresh the affected goldens locally (keyless web snapshot refresh) and keep the card badge at this layer: the client list that labels it experimental arrives with the client layer.

* docs(liveshare): mark the shipping owner policy note implemented

The protocol-and-owner-surfaces decision shipped with this bundle, so the note moves from proposed/ to implemented/ in both languages, its proposal-era headings become Decision/Verification/Consequences, and the subsystem page plus package README link to the new path. The pairing record moves with the triplet.

* fix(liveshare): judge tool turns from the open Session turn and recheck the narrowed write

The master baseline has no ToolExecutionInput.turn, so the host derives the turn a tool execution serves from the Agent's Session: the latest turn/start with no turn/end after it. A missing Agent, Session, or open turn yields no turn and the fork guard refuses the execution (fail-closed) instead of reading it as the owner's. Also refuse a fork that names a child without a bound rpcId/operationId, classify forwarded paths by their normalized pathname so /api/session/./fork or a query suffix cannot skip the fork decision, and ask the write gate again after the final authorization refresh so a share narrowed to view during fs/write-intent cannot write. The subsystem page, package README, and model-experience census follow the two-tier model and the bounded-write child ceiling.

* refactor(liveshare): read the open turn beside the requester fold

The derivation reads the same Session log the requester fold decides, so it
lives with that fold and the host imports it instead of keeping a private copy.

* test(liveshare): cover the derived turn and the refusal paths

Drive the host's real derivation from Session events: the open turn of the
Agent's Session decides a viewer turn is confined and an owner turn is not,
while a missing Agent, an absent open turn, and a requester the host no longer
drives all refuse instead of being read as the owner's. Cover the three safety
behaviours the host commit added: fork child naming without a bound request
identity, dot-segment/query fork paths that must still reach the fork decision,
and a share narrowed to view while fs/write-intent awaits.

* fix(liveshare): avoid the deprecated snapshot reader and the extra casts

The host derived the open turn by scanning the Session event log, which the
deprecation note forbids for new production calls. Read the same state from the
turnBoundary projection the Agents service maintains instead, and let a spec
supply a fixture boundary reader where production supplies turnBoundaryOf.
The live attribution of an execution is unchanged: an absent boundary or one
between turns still yields no turn and the guard refuses it fail-closed.

* docs(liveshare): describe the bundle's indirect model experience

The bundle's Model Experience moved to the audited indirect classification,
so the README sentence now names the path: viewer prompts the owner host
forwards into a shared Session drive that Session's model requests. The
KV-cache paragraph and the bilingual pairing record follow.

* test(liveshare): pin the turn-start admission for steered and admitted reader input

The pre-step admission already re-reads Relay authority from each entering message's own source and refuses queued reader input whose grant ended before the model runs; the new cases pin the steer path and the admitted viewer turn, so the turn-start half stays proven next to the delivery-time recheck the Session Controller owns.

* test(liveshare): adapt the replay and cancel expectations to the parsed tier

* test(liveshare): align the access-state expectations with protocol v2

The parsed share-access-state frame always carries allowsFileUpload, the
withdrawn fork-readonly word no longer implies a view tier or forking, and a
hand-built frame may not name it. Update the hand-built expectations and the
two fixture specs that named the retired word, without touching production
semantics.

* test(liveshare): record the in-flight cancel race after the controller revert

The Session Controller no longer re-reads a caller's access before cancelling,
so a cancel admitted before the reader's grant ends keeps its effect. State that
as the known limitation the earlier refusal tests documented instead.

* feat(liveshare): add the viewer attachment-upload switch

The share record, registration handshake, access-state replay, and share-viewer
policy carry an owner switch that is off by default: it admits fileUploads/upload
on the shared Session and the viewer's own forks, is independent of the tier and
of forking, and is normalized to off at every untrusted state-file or frame
boundary.

* docs(liveshare): state the sandbox tiers and the attachment switch

Name the two execution tiers as a read-only sandbox and a bounded writable
sandbox, and document the independent default-off switch that lets admitted
viewers upload attachments, including that legacy shares read as off.

* refactor(liveshare): drop the withdrawn fork-readonly migration

The feature never shipped, so no stored record can name the withdrawn tier and
the boundary needs no compatibility path. Read a stored fork switch as exactly
what it states, let an old Relay state the switch explicitly instead of
inferring it from the tier, and stop accepting the retired mode name on create
or restore.

* fix(liveshare): preflight a resumed child's limit before publishing it

A resumed child is announced through agent/created before its execution limit
installs, so an installability failure left a created Session whose guard never
landed. Resolve the recorded child's granted workspace before activation and
refuse the resume there, so a child this host cannot confine is never published.

* refactor(liveshare): render the viewer page through the reader's own Peer

The served-page seam now hands the frontend reader the reader's Peer, which renders that page's own
opening access rows; the Liveshare side no longer assembles a global access snapshot and the removed
global is gone. The viewer read service builds the same Peer it already creates for every dispatch and
passes it to the asset reader.

* fix(liveshare): keep the owner upload switch across an older Relay's access frame

The Relay is the authority for what a viewer receives, but only for the fields its frame states. An
older Relay predates the upload switch and omits it entirely; the protocol parser rightly normalizes a
missing switch to off for frames that state it, so the host must inspect the raw answer to tell not

* test(liveshare): adapt the host specs to the current tool and session APIs

The host specs drove a single tool through the pre-batch executor shape and handed
some tests a Session outside its store; the current tool executor takes a call batch
and Session appends require the owning SessionStore. This adapts those fixtures to
the current shapes without changing what each test asserts.

Also gives the reader's own fork the same Session permissions as the source grant:
forking its own child again and renaming it are allowed on the child only, while the
source Session still refuses renaming and keeps forking as its one Session verb.

* fix(liveshare): let the owner's background turns run while a share is served

The requester fold only counts a message with `source.kind === 'user'`, so a
turn a background event opened has no attributable input and stayed `unknown`;
the source-session tool guard refused every tool in that turn. Establish the
owner's own turn for an input-less turn and leave unattributable input unknown.

* fix(liveshare): grant the reader its own fork's rename and gate child forks by the fork switch

* refactor(liveshare): read the served page through webServer.readResource

* feat(boot): offer the Liveshare host bundle from the official bundle list

`@deepseek-ai/dsh-official-bundles` owns the shipped template, retired, and
optional bundle lists now, so the liveshare bundle joins `OPTIONAL_BUNDLES`
there instead of being restated in the app-boot profile module.

* feat(liveshare): gate the reader's own fork independently of its input permissions

The reader's child gets prompt, cancel, and rename from a role with no extra
condition, while forking the shared Session or one of the reader's own forks
belongs to a separate role bound to the owner's fork switch. A viewer cannot
rename the shared Session, and a withdrawn fork switch also withdraws forking
a child.

* test(liveshare): adapt the admission specs to the current tool and driver APIs

* feat(liveshare): accept only the declarations a plugin's own package owns

A viewer plugin may contribute endpoints a share can offer, so a declaration
has to name a live Host Remote endpoint whose generated id belongs to the
declaring package. Fail closed: no loader entry, no local endpoint, no owning
package, or a foreign owner all refuse the declaration, and the recorded
attribution is the package name the owner sees.

The package's Typert artifact registers after its apply runs, so a plugin
declares once that registration has happened.

* feat(liveshare): classify every Remote endpoint before the reader policy decides it

The share-viewer policy refuses by default, so the endpoints it decides were a
handwritten whitelist that could drift from the generated endpoint set. State
every endpoint's reason in one shared table: the Client face proves it covers
`RemoteEndpoint` (both directions), the Host derives `POLICY_DECIDED_ACTIONS`
from the reader entries, and a load-time assertion fails if the derived set and
the roles' actions disagree.

* fix(liveshare): declare the Client face its classification gate compiles in

Typert attributes a package's exports to a face only for manifests declaring
`dsh.client` plus a `./client` subpath (`isDualFacePackage`). Without that row
the client catalog read `exports["."]` — the Host entry — from the Client
program, which holds only the classification table and its completeness gate,
and failed on the source that program does not contain.

Export the gate module as `./client`, declare the Client row, publish its
bundle, and exempt the package from Client/Host dependency treatment: the
runtime importing these dependencies is the Host's, and `dsh.client` here only
attributes the compilation face.

* test(liveshare): align worker fixtures with the protocol tenant contract

The protocol layer rejects a share RPC actor whose tenant is empty at the IPC ingress. The worker fixtures still described a peer normalizing the tenant to an empty string, so the Host dropped every fabricated request event and the lifecycle and correlation polls timed out. Use a concrete tenant in the fixtures; those scenarios do not depend on an empty tenant.

* chore(docs): count the liveshare persistence nodes in the format index

The regenerated current-checkout catalog adds the liveshare viewer-principal nodes, so the v4 row's node count moves from 622 to 626. Refresh the generated format index rather than keeping the pre-liveshare count.

* refactor(liveshare): consume the protocol package's single public entry

The wait is bounded at 600 s (DSH_REMOTE_BRIDGE_TURN_END_QUIET_MAX_MS),
cleared on dispose, and books the rate windows at the real send. A new turn
the bridge can see starting drops the held end.

fix(remote-bridge): read a new turn only from increments that prove one

Any increment that was not a turn end counted as "a turn started", which the
follow stream does not support: a child's settle notice arrives on the parent as
a user message with an agent actor, and usage counts and catalog changes arrive
at the end of a turn. A turn ending while its child still ran therefore had its
held announcement dropped the moment that child settled, which is the case the
quiet gate exists for.

isTurnStartDelta now names the evidence once, for the connection drain and the
standing watchers alike: streaming assistant work, and a user message this
session's own user wrote. The watcher note's reporting bullet states the
shipped ordering and log line again.
merge(remote-bridge): announce a turn end once the session is quiet

fix(remote-bridge): deliver an event once per APNs token, not once per row

One iPhone held the same APNs token on two roster rows and got two identical
notifications: pair.finish enrolls on every accept, enroll minted a row per
accept instead of reusing the one its fingerprint already owned, registerPush
only wrote the connected device's row, and #announce admitted the event once by
(sessionId, event) and then sent it once per target.

The sender now converges its targets by deviceToken before fan-out, enroll
reuses the row a fingerprint already has and moves only the credential, and a
load compacts the table to one row per fingerprint and one registration per
token, writing the result back through the roster's serialized queue. The
schema stays version 2, no frame, capability or topic changes, and the three
existing push limits keep their values.

Both READMEs state the two rules and the note records the rejected paths.

fix(market): retry a throttled Cloudflare API in the deploy lane

The Deploy Market lane failed three times on dev (runs 40350674320,
40367640238, 40430514377) about a second into scripts/deploy-market:
wrangler's first request, GET /accounts/{account}/workers/services/
dsh-market, came back 429 Too Many Requests with no Retry-After header,
and wrangler only backs off when that header is present, so the deploy
died on the first throttled response.

Every wrangler invocation now runs under a bounded retry policy:
MAX_ATTEMPTS = 4 with 5s / 20s / 60s between them. Only transient
conditions are retried - HTTP 429, HTTP 5xx in the shapes wrangler
prints, "malformed response from the API", and socket-level errors -
while a bad config, a rejected token, a missing binding or a
non-transient D1 error keeps the old fail-fast path and the byte
identical message. When the budget is spent the failure carries the
reason, the attempt count, the Cloudflare Ray ID and a bounded tail of
the captured output, and the child's output still reaches the job log
as it happens.

The lane's other gates are unchanged: the market-build preflight, the
D1 migration step, the TURNSTILE_SECRET and ASSET_ATTEST_SECRET
fail-closed checks, the siteverify pairing probe and every exit code.
scripts/deploy-market.test.mjs drives the policy through injected
attempts and waits (no sleeping, no network) plus two real-child cases
for the output relay and the stdin payload.

Two behaviours the family settings card got wrong, both reported by the
suite that landed with the coverage scoping change:

apply.revert() for Escape and then blurs the input, and the blur
handler called apply.commit(), so one Escape reported a discard and
then a save; Enter double-committed for the same reason. ValueField
now remembers that Enter or Escape settled the draft, and the blur they
cause no longer writes again, while a real focus change still commits.

renderChildrenWhenNotExposed suppressed the notice. A card that keeps
its rows when the host does not serve the namespace rendered the rows
with no explanation that the namespace is missing. The not-exposed
paragraph is hoisted above the branch, so it explains the rows too, and
hideNotExposedNotice still hides it wherever it would render.

notice, and fail on the old code. shared/client/settings is the source:
the eight consumer copies are regenerated by scripts/sync-shared.mjs
(sync-shared --check passes), and dsh-market's committed lib/ artifacts
and scripts/lib-artifact-fingerprints.json are rebuilt with pnpm build

fix(liangshen): page tool_activate from the catalog's published partition

Under the default `ptc` presentation the catalog installs
`agent.ctx.tools.restrict({deny})` before the request assembles, so the paged
families are already gone from every scoped reader. `tool_activate` recomputed
the page from `agent.ctx.tools.schemas(agent)` and therefore found an empty
page ("paged namespaces in this session: (none)") while the same request's
catalog advertised those namespaces — every MCP namespace was unreachable in
production, and the native presentation was the only path that worked because
no restriction is installed there.

Publish the pre-restriction partition from the paging sync and read it back in
the activation tool, so the catalog message and the tool that loads a namespace
come from one fact. The schema read stays as the fallback for scopes nothing
pages: native presentation, a deployment without the catalog row, or a test
stub.

Covered by a regression test that mounts both preset rows on one registry and
activates through the restricted scope; disabling the published-partition
branch turns it red.

docs(liangshen): state the regression test's shared scope precisely

The activation row's own ctx is a capture stub; what it shares with the catalog
is the restricted registry the agent scope points at. The earlier comment
claimed both rows were "mounted on one registry", which overstated the fixture.

feat(task-board): clear labels whose tasks have all settled

The label manager could rename and delete one label at a time, so a label kept
alive by an old experiment stayed in the filter row until someone hunted it down
row by row. Cleanup adds a threshold (5 by default, 1..99) and judges the whole
ledger: a label is a candidate when fewer tasks than that carry it and every one
of them is done or failed. Archived cards are counted on the same terms, so a
card that is archived and still unfinished holds its label back.

Candidates are computed before anything is written: with none the row only says
so and leaves the ledger alone, and with some it asks for confirmation listing
each label with the number of tasks carrying it. Each accepted label then leaves
through the existing delete-tag ledger transition, so cleanup adds no wire action
and no second write path.

The label-management decision record owns the rule and records the two rejected
shapes (a batch wire action, an automatic sweep); the task-tags note's "no
cleanup entry" line was stale and now points at the manager.

feat(task-board): carry the label clear rule on a corner question mark

The clear control acts on the whole ledger, so trailing the label list made it
read as the last row's action. It now sits in the card header beside the title,
and the rule it explains moves out of the body: a round `?` holds the sentence as
its native title (the convention every icon button here already uses) and as an
aria-describedby description kept visually hidden, so the corner stays two
controls wide while a pointer, a keyboard and a screen reader all still get the
rule. The "nothing matched" notice stays supporting text in the body, where a
status line belongs, rather than travelling with the control.

The corner cluster reuses the existing contracts — .scheduleZone for the labeled
threshold field, .ghostButton for the commit — and adds only the help button plus
the hidden-text utility. Assertions pin the new shape: the `?` carries the hint
as title and description, and both it and the commit live in the header.

docs(task-board): state what the corner question mark actually reaches

A native title renders on pointer hover only; the hidden description is what
covers assistive technology. The comment claimed keyboard parity it does not
have, and recorded why a styled tooltip was rejected (the modal clips overflow).

fix(dsh-agents): run an unbound squad in the Host default directory

The workspace registry was read once while the row applied, but the official
registry's Service.init is asynchronous and finishes afterwards, so the face
stayed undefined for the life of the process. Both halves then failed: the state
view offered no workspace to pick (the form degraded to a typed id) and every
run that pinned one answered workspace-unavailable.

- resolve ctx.workspaceRegistry per call, like the llm face beside it
- make the pin optional: an unbound squad opens its session with no workspaceId
  and the Host composes it in its own default directory; a pin that is set still
  fails closed with workspace-unavailable or workspace-unknown
- drop the unreachable workspace-required code and its status mapping
- render the squad workspace as a picker even when no registry is reported, and
  keep a pin the registry does not list visible instead of silently clearing it
- realign the model-facing tool descriptions, both READMEs, the remote-bridge
  error-code enum and the Agent Note that owned the refusal list

fix(task-board): let a modal title shrink instead of overlapping its corner

The label manager now puts a fixed-width cluster in the header, so a title
without overflow handling could paint over it — visible with the longer
localised titles, not with the two-character Chinese one.

feat(task-board): move the label manager's whole rule onto its question mark

The body kept a second explanation after the clear rule moved to the corner —
what labels are and what renaming or deleting does to the cards. Both sentences
now travel on the one `?` beside the title (native title, so the modal's own
overflow cannot clip it), and the body is the list alone, with the "nothing
matched" notice where a status line belongs.

The key follows what it now means: tags.cleanupHelp becomes tags.help, since the
control explains the dialog rather than the clear rule. Assertions cover the
merged text on both title and description and check that no rendered paragraph
still carries either sentence — the copy in the DOM is only the visually hidden
description.

test(dsh-agents): pin the workspace registry resolution at the apply seam

The original defect lived in the wiring, not in the service: a face captured
while the row applied stayed undefined because the official registry's
Service.init is asynchronous. Every other assertion sat one layer below it, so
re-introducing the capture as a closure kept the whole suite green.

The new case applies the real row against a cordis Host that serves no
workspaceRegistry, then provides one from a sibling fiber, and asserts both the
offered list in the state view and the pinned id reaching session/create.
Reverting index.ts to an apply-time capture fails it; the comment on the page's
workspace helper is realigned with the always-a-picker behaviour beside it.

fix(liangshen): replay activations dispatched from inside a program

Under the ptc presentation the wire carries run_code alone, so tool_activate is
reached from inside a program and the harness records tool/ptc-dispatch — no
top-level tool/call is ever written. replayActivations read only tool/call, so
the active set was always empty: every activation reported success, the page
never lifted, the same namespace could be activated again for ever, and the MCP
families stayed unreachable no matter how many times the model asked for them.

Both event shapes now feed the same recency list in session order, and an errored
dispatch activates nothing, the same rule the tool/result pairing already used.
Proven against a real session log: replaying production events yields the activated
namespaces, while the same log with dispatch events removed yields none.

Unit cases cover a successful and an errored dispatch; an integration case drives
the whole loop — dispatch recorded, catalog replays it, scope stops withholding.

fix(dsh-agents): read the settled command record, not the handler result

The official dispatcher answers { commandId, result } for every settled command.
The permission pin read kind off that record, so result.kind was always
undefined and every successful switch was reported as "the permission command
failed" — which is why a squad member with a pinned permission could never be
launched, while a member without one ran fine.

The task board already unwraps the record this way; this brings the run gateway
to the same contract. The new cases pin all three outcomes: the success record,
a refused preset whose own text must survive, and a Host that acknowledges
nothing.

fix(task-board): paint the label manager's rule as a bubble, not a title

Hovering the corner question mark showed nothing: Electron's renderer does not
paint a native title here. The rule is now a real element anchored under the
button — inside the modal box this stylesheet clips — revealed on hover and on
focus-within, so a keyboard user gets it too, and it stays the element
aria-describedby names. No native title remains on the control, so a browser that
does paint titles cannot show a second, duplicate tooltip.

The bubble is deliberately wide: a short modal must not clip its last line.

fix(task-board): open the rule bubble rightwards so the card cannot clip it

A right-anchored bubble ran off the modal's left edge and .modal clipped the start
of both sentences ("标签是顶…", "任务数少…"). The ? sits just left of the clear
control, so the bubble now anchors to the ?'s left edge and opens rightwards at a
width that stays inside the card in every shipped locale.

fix(dsh-agents): stop shipping host core packages as runtime dependencies

dsh-agents declared @deepseek-ai/dsh-brand, dsh-session-persistence and
dsh-session-projection in dependencies with the prerelease range
^0.2.1-rc.3. The plugin manager installs that section into the user

became a version switch nobody asked for: ^0.2.1-rc.3 equals
>=0.2.1-rc.3 <0.3.0-0, the next rc of the same 0.2.1 cohort satisfies it,

the running host supplies. sessionProjections then never registers,
agent-loop fails activation, and every plugin waiting on that service

lets the host supply the runtime copy; the single host peer
"@deepseek-ai/dsh": ">=<cohort>" already records the version requirement.

explicitly, and add scripts/family-host-dependencies.test.mjs so a family
package cannot put a host core package back into dependencies.

npm users keep the shipped 0.4.11 manifest until a patch release carries
this change; the profile-side workaround is a pnpm-workspace overrides
block pinning the four core packages.

fix(git): harden runGit's output caps — latch, killTree, stderr budget

dev already caps stdout bytes (GIT_OUTPUT_MAX_BYTES) and NUL fields, but
three gaps remain, all proven by the 2026-10-13 host crashes (twice:
RangeError: Invalid string length at the stdout accumulator, a junction-
forest workspace driving 'git status -uall' to gigabytes):

1. no latch after a byte-cap reject — later chunks kept ACCUMULATING on
   the retained strings. On Windows spawn('git') resolves to the cmd
   shim, whose grandchild survives child.kill() and keeps feeding the
   dead accumulator (measured: the orphan outlived kill() by 20+s). The
   fieldCapped guard covered only the row cap; the byte cap had none.
2. kill() reaches only the wrapper — the orphaned grandchild needs its
   pipes destroyed (EPIPE) to actually stop. killTree() destroys both
   streams and is now used by every kill path (timeout, byte cap, field
   cap).
3. stderr was uncapped — a command whose DIAGNOSTICS stream past the
   budget is as able to kill the host via string length as its answer;
   stderr now shares the same maxBytes budget.

Worst case in a pathological workspace is now one failed SCM refresh,
never a dead host.

fix(editor): remember the edit scroll position across tab re-seating

Saving re-seats the native tab body (the chip's dirty mark clears, the change
gutter refreshes), and a scroller that is detached from the document comes back
with `scrollTop` 0 — scroll position is carried neither by React state nor by
the DOM node, so the edit surface needed its own memory. The preview already
kept one for the same reason (its save-then-reload collapses the container);
the editor relied on the view never being re-seated, which saving breaks.

Mirror the preview's pattern for the CodeMirror scroller:

- record the position on the scroller's scroll event, keyed per session + path,
  with a guard so the restore's own write is not recorded as the user's;
- restore on the save edges (`saving → saved`, the change-gutter refresh, the
  mode gate), and after every reveal re-measure moved from #890's family;
- skip when the document fits (no meaningful position) or when the position did
  not change.

On top of the upstream `dev` line that already carries #859 and #890.

fix(sidechat): trim the seed when a model switch rewrites the head

A model switch after the last compaction replaces the protected system
prompt with a system/message whose seq sits after the cut but whose
surface slot is the head before the checkpoint. The builder refused that
shape, so every such sidechat copied the parent log in full.

Resolve the single-node replacement chain to its pre-cut anchor using the
checkpoint's recorded shadowed set (not its declared numeric range, which
misclassifies keep-window replacements), carry the latest replacement in
the head slot with the anchor's turn/step scaffolding, and consume the
chain so the keep window and tail never re-emit it. Range replacements,
targets the checkpoint removed, non-system nodes, and broken or forward
chains still fall back to the verbatim copy.

Tests cover a single switch, a two-switch chain, a multi-hop chain whose
intermediate sits inside the declared range but not in the shadowed set,
and a valid range fallback. The trim fixtures fall back on the old code.
Real parent logs now trim (6036->187, 8329->2479, 16458->4359, ...) with
surface equivalence and Session.create acceptance; the previous
35992->3456 trim is unchanged.

perf(sidebar): give every consumer one stable session scope

A tab body keys memos and effects off `scope` (the diff pane resolves its
media/html routes from it, the editor restores its preview scroll, the side
chat rebuilds its prose-rewrite cache), but the tab cell built
`{ sessionId, cwd }` fresh on every render. Every such dependency therefore
looked changed whenever the cell re-rendered — which the memo comparator
allows exactly when a COMPARED field moves: `expanded` on a directory toggle,
plus `revealed`, `localeRevision`, `tabsVersion`. The diff preview then
re-ran its whole-document rewrite and its content tab re-issued a whole-file
`fs.read`, flashing its loading row.

`useSessionScope` is now the one place a scope for a component tree is built;
the tab cell, the diff tab, the native tab adapter, and the shell's badge /
rightActions / `+` menu / lifecycle-callback seams all use it. Those last
ones are documented external plug-in surfaces, so a plug-in memoizing on
`scope` stops churning on every unrelated re-render too.

Stabilizing the object removes the only path the diff pane's `content` tab
had to re-read after the file changed on disk, so the header's refresh button
now drives it explicitly (the pane owns the gesture; the loader no longer
leaks its internal counter).

Seven comments asserted that the scope object's identity churns on every
render; that premise is gone, so the ones that still apply say what they
actually guard.

host already caches completed cold reads by persistence revision), and the

fix(host): root a detached session at its stored header, not a full log read

cwdOf() resolves the cwd for every file/Git route, and a cold (detached)
session paid one host observation per call: sessionQuery.observeSession({
projectionMode: 'all' }) decodes the whole zstd artifact and hydrates every
projection to answer with one workingDirectory string. The 0.28.1
single-flight only covered /sidebar/api, while the real startup fan-out
never goes through it: the fs-watch socket sends one frame PER WATCHED
DIRECTORY (server resolves cwd before it even reads the op), /sidebar/file
and /sidebar/html resolve per resource, upload/write per call. A 39 MB
session was therefore decoded dozens of times in parallel — the 44-read
OOM on 0.28.0 and the 36 reads reported against 0.28.1 are the same path,
not a broken dedupe.

A detached session now resolves through sessionPersistence.stat(), which
reads the first zstd frame only (header-only, never the log), memoized per
session id (headers are immutable) and shared in-flight across concurrent
asks. activeWorktreeRootOf() answers a detached session with that address
and no longer folds the stored log. Once the host attaches the session the
committed working_directory and linked-worktree following resume as before.

Trade-off (documented): until attach, the sidebar roots at the original
project rather than the agent's last directory/worktree.

feat(mnemon): move the data directory from the settings page

The settings page's **data directory** field recorded a path and nothing
more: memory read and wrote the new location from then on, and whatever was
already in the old one stayed there, which the README stated outright. A
directory that differs from the one memory uses is now offered as a move.
The field opens the shell's own directory chooser where the shell has one
and stays typable where it does not, and the confirmation dialog reads the
source first and names both paths, the files and bytes it would carry, and
the fact that nothing is deleted before every file verifies.

Moving is a Host operation of its own — `storage-plan` and `storage-migrate`
on the Pack channel — because the runtime that holds every component has to
be rebuilt on the new directory before the call returns. The plan reports
what the source holds, whether the target already carries Mnemon data, and
whether the two roots share a device; a move refuses a target that is
occupied, nested in or identical to the source, or a filesystem root on
either side, and a profile that cannot be written is refused before any file
is copied.

On one device the move is a single rename. Across devices the tree is copied
and every file is read back and compared by SHA-256 before the source
directory is removed, so a failed verification leaves the original untouched.
A completed move records the new path as the `custom` data directory and
rebuilds the runtime on it, so the page, the Pack backup and every component
read the new directory without a restart.

Choosing **Default** stops memory from *using* a custom directory instead of
forgetting which one was chosen, so the choice can be taken back, and the
field keeps whatever was typed.

docs: describe the directory chooser, the move confirmation and the two endpoints.

docs(mnemon): record the data-directory move on the settings page

The move is a user-visible change, so the pull request needs the same evidence
the other feature work carries: the row on Default, the field and the shell's

Captured from a real `dsh web` instance served by scripts/serve-e2e.mjs with a
disposable profile. The directory in the images is that fixture's own throwaway
root; no personal memory or credential appears in any of them. The move dialog
itself needs a native chooser this headless fixture cannot serve, so it stays
covered by tests/client-storage-review.spec.tsx and tests/storage-migration.spec.ts.

feat(skills): let the draft and backtest pages pick the model that runs the work

Drafting a suggestion and backtesting a skill always ran on whatever route the
task Agent happened to inherit, so there was no way to try a cheaper or a
stronger model for one page, one suggestion, or one skill.

Both pages now offer a global pick and an optional per-item override: an
override per suggestion on 进化, and one per skill on 评测, each falling back to
the page's global pick and then to the task Agent's own route. The picks live in
a `preferences.json` beside the ledger — deliberately outside the ledger
fingerprint, so changing a pick does not invalidate an open page's revision.

The Host carries the pick down to the agent it starts. While doing so it stops
forwarding the inherited `reasoningEffort`: a Provider spells its levels in its
own words, so passing one Provider's `max` to another that has no such level
made the run die with UNSUPPORTED_REASONING_EFFORT. The picked Provider now
decides its own effort unless the pick names one.

Two related repairs come with it, because the pages could not be used without
them. A suggestion whose draft write died with the previous Host stays in
`drafting` forever and refuses both a retry and a delete; the store now puts
such a suggestion back to `pending` with an explanation, both when the ledger is
read and once when the source starts. And a suggestion or a draft can be deleted
from its card, which is what the drafting state was blocking.

The model selectors also repeat the chosen Provider under the model name, and
flip their menu above the button when there is no room below: the menu is
clamped into the viewport by measuring the selector before it opens, so a long
directory no longer covers the button it belongs to.

对比灵枢智能论 v3.4 与外部《缓存感知的记忆注入架构 v6.0》（level0000x）：

开关分片句柄。客户端 60s 超时衡量整条链，卡在这里就把「已落盘但没回话」读成失败，

  与写路径以 _dirty_lock 互斥（只护字典、**不含 IO**）；close()/atexit 仍同步落盘并

fix(ui): payload 钉 eol=lf——Windows checkout 的 CRLF 会让安装器判「分享包损坏」而拒装

病象（本机 0.9.14 实测）：`ui/minimal/install.ps1 -PluginPath <插件> -CheckOnly` 直接报
  分享包文件缺失或损坏：web/index.html
而该文件实际存在、内容完好。

根因（第4条取证，不猜测）：安装器对 payload **逐文件校验 sha256**（`ui/minimal/integrity.json`
按 LF 记录），而 `ui/minimal/payload/**` 未在 `.gitattributes` 钉行尾 ⇒ Windows 默认
`core.autocrlf=true` checkout 后 payload 变 CRLF ⇒ `Get-FileHash` 与清单失配 ⇒ 拒绝安装。

铁证（9 个 payload 文件逐一核对）：
  · `git show HEAD:` 的内容与清单 sha256 **逐字节一致**（9/9）⇒ 清单本身没坏；
  · 工作树原始字节比对清单：**9/9 不符**，且 9/9 文件的每处 LF 前都有 CR（纯 CRLF）；
  · 把工作树字节 LF 化后重算：**9/9 相符**。

修法：`.gitattributes` 增 `ui/minimal/payload/** text eol=lf`——与既有 `*.sh` / `*.yml` 钉 LF
同款理由：这些文件的行尾是**判据对象**（hash 校验），跨平台字节一致才算兼容。

验证（灵枢 0.9.14）：
  · 归一工作树后 `-CheckOnly` rc=0：兼容性与完整性检查通过，计划修改 12 个文件；
  · 临时副本实装 rc=0：新增 9 文件 + `dsh.client` 注入（sidebar 三依赖）+
    `installConsoleWeb(ctx, config, disposers, mdcg)` 调用点就位；
  · 幂等：再次执行「此插件已安装本 UI，无需重复安装」，文件数不变；
  · 卸载：逐文件恢复，**快照 == 初始**（逐字节等价）；卸载后 `-CheckOnly` 再次通过；
  · 真机在役插件（`D:\dsh-home\profiles\web\...\dsh-memory` 0.9.14）实装 rc=0：
    9 文件就位、`dsh.client` 注入、备份 `records=12` 可回滚。

feat(writegate): 分层写入严格度闸——情景层可放宽、知识/结构/自我逐层加严、自我层需人工

裁定（2026-10-27，使用者原话）：「记忆写入是要有，但是得经过复核。至于放宽的写入情况，
则应该是没有子代理可以用，且没有蜂巢，智能体团队功能时。可以写入情景层。知识，结构，
自我层，一层要比一层严格。自我人格的偏移，失忆，是毁灭性的。」

实现（新模块 `md_cg/writegate.py` + `security.require_layer_write` 接入）：

| 档 | 层 | 有复核通道时需 |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | `contextual` / `goals` / `unresolved` / `rejected` | 无要求；**无任何通道时也允许直写**（裁定的放宽通道） |
| 1 | `knowledge` | 反思单元 |
| 2 | `structural` | 反思 + 验证 |
| 3 | `self` / `anchor` | 反思 + 验证 + **人工裁定** |

- `review_channels()`：从 `MDCG_REVIEW_CHANNELS`（hive/subagent/team）读取可用复核通道；
  为空 ⇒ 视为「无复核能力」⇒ **只准写 0 档**，1 档以上一律 deny 并点名缺失单元；
- 三档开关 `MDCG_WRITE_GATE`：**`off`（缺省，完全不介入）** / `warn`（记录并放行）/ `enforce`（阻断）；
  非法值 fail-open 到 off 并告警一次；
- 未知层按 2 档保守处理（宁严不松）；
- 与既有闸门正交：`PROTECTED_LAYERS` 管「已存在受保护节点不许改删」，本闸管「新写/覆写某层要不要复核」；
  `can_write`/`layers_allow`/`clearance` 仍是硬权限，本闸只追加**程序性**要求。

为什么缺省 off：一升级就阻断会立刻自伤（自动记忆写入全部落 knowledge 层）。
故先留观察档 warn，由使用者显式切 enforce。

验证：`md_cg/test_writegate_tiers.py` **30 通过 / 0 失败**：
  · A 档位归一（含非法值 fail-open）与四档递增、未知层保守、锚点=自我同档；
  · B **无通道**时四个 0 档层可写、四个 1+ 档层被拒并点名缺失单元；
  · C 有通道时逐档判定（知识只需反思；结构缺验证被点名；自我层双单元仍不够，须人工）；
  · D 三档语义（off 连自我层也放行；warn 判定同形由调用方决定；通道声明解析）；
  · E 接入锚点（off 提前返回、enforce 才抛、reviewers 环境声明）。

诚实边界：
- 本闸只认「复核单元声明」，不做证据真伪校验（真伪由蜂巢/子代理侧签章承接）；
- `enforce` 下当前环境若无通道，**知识层以上一律拒写**——包括自动记忆归档；
  上线前须先声明 `MDCG_REVIEW_CHANNELS` 或接受只写情景层；
- 未改 `MdCGSecure.add` 之外任何写入路径的签名（`reviewers` 为可选形参，缺省读环境）。

偏差（第4条取证 + 第0.4条如实登记）：我把 `MDCG_REVIEW_CHANNELS` 的**空值**当成

    subagent_fork），`web` profile 的 bundles 也含 `@deepseek-ai/dsh-subagent-codex`、

  · 派了一个只读子代理任务，**跑通**（exit 0，stdout `subagent-channel-ok`，未改任何文件）。

  ② **文案越界**：deny reason 原文写「无复核通道（无子代理/无蜂巢/无智能体团队）」——
     本层根本不知道子代理/蜂巢/团队是否存在，却把「没声明」写成了「不存在」。

    写情景层」；
  · 模块头补边界注释：本变量是部署声明，**声明缺失 ≠ 能力缺失**；

    探测子代理」——本模块属大脑库、跨 harness 复用，能力只有各端自己知道；
  · 守卫新增 F 组 4 条：未声明时只报「未声明」且提示「声明缺失不等于能力缺失」、
    声明 subagent 后被如实回报、deny 用「未声明」、**deny 文案禁含能力断言**
    （`无子代理`/`无蜂巢` 一律不得出现在 reason 里——这正是这次误报的源头）。

验证：`md_cg/test_writegate_tiers.py` **34 通过 / 0 失败**（A/B/C/D/E/F 六组）。

  · 子代理：可用（实测）；蜂巢：不可用（serve 未起 + 缺 HIVE_API_KEY）；
  · 智能体团队：**未验证**（此前被我与子代理混为一谈，不再下结论）。

fix(hive): serve 配置的 {"env":…} 增机器级回落——DSH 子进程拿不到机器级变量时不再误报「未设」

病象（2026-10-27 现场）：`hive/serve_start.py` 拉起 serve 时报
  `配置项解析失败（来源 env 未设或文件不可读）：HIVE_API_KEY`
调用方（DSH 端代理）据此判定「蜂巢不可用」而全程降级——**误判**。

根因（第4条取证）：
  · `hive/config.local.json` 的 `HIVE_API_KEY` 写成 `{"env": "DEEPSEEK_API_KEY"}`，
    解析的是**调用进程**的环境变量；
  · DSH 主进程启动早于该变量设置（或环境被清理），其子进程（插件/MCP）继承不到；
  · 而 Windows **机器级**（HKLM Session Manager\Environment）里该变量**存在**（35 字符）；
  · `resolve()` 只读进程 env ⇒ 取空 ⇒ `load_config` 判 bad ⇒ fail fast。

修法（最小、只读、显式优先）：
  · 新增 `_machine_env(name)`：仅 Windows，读 HKLM 机器级同名变量；非 Windows 直接 None；
  · `resolve({"env": X})`：先读进程 env，**为空才**经 `_machine_env` 回落；
    进程 env 里显式设置过的值**优先**（便于临时覆盖，不被打回机器级）；
  · 两者皆空仍返回 None ⇒ `load_config` 的 **fail fast 语义不变**（残缺 env 的 serve 仍不上岗）。

验证：新增守卫 `hive/test_serve_env_fallback.py` **12 通过 / 0 失败**：
  · A 三形态（直值/进程 env/file）不变；**两者皆空仍 None**（fail fast 保留）；
  · B 机器级可读、未知名 None、进程空时回落值一致、**显式进程 env 优先于机器级**；
  · C `load_config` 两态（正常通过 / 解析不到仍点名 fail fast）+ 本机真实
    `config.local.json` 全键可解析（含机器级回落的 `HIVE_API_KEY`）。

实测效果：修后同一调用方直接 `serve_start.start(config.local.json)` 成功
（`ok:true`，pid 11480，workers 4），`hive_doctor` 报 `serve_alive: true`、
`serve_env_source.api_key_set: true`，积压任务 `h_dsh端_灵枢迭代_验证单元_0022`
随即被领取（running）。

为什么不需要同时改 DSH 侧配置：MCP 的 `hive_mcp` 首次拉起 serve 也走同一个
`load_config`，故本修法一处覆盖两条拉起路径；且 `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` 只有 hive 用，
灵枢插件本身不需要它——避免把密钥写进宿主配置（第9条）。

# 根因（反思单元归因 · 验证单元交叉核验 · 主代理代码确认）

`md_cg/docindex.py` 的 `walk` 只对 `filenames` 排序，**`dirnames` 保持 `os.scandir` 原始顺序**。
而 readdir 顺序：**Windows/NTFS 按名、Linux（ext4/overlayfs/tmpfs）不保证**。

于是兄弟目录 `private/`（应 fail-closed）与 `public/`（正常落库）**谁先被遍历**随平台变：

- Windows：按名 → `private` 先 → 抛 `AccessDenied` 时**尚未落任何库** → 测试 A3 的 `not _sb` 绿；
- Linux：可能 `public` 先 → 公开文档先落库 → `_sb` 非空 → A3 的 `not _sb` **红**。

这解释了「CI 单条红 / 本机全绿 / 重跑即绿」的全部现象，也解释了「三次 flake 不同源但同工法」：
把「实现的一次具体执行」写成等值断言，而不是写成不变量。

# 修法（三层）

1. **确定性**（治根因）：`docindex.py` 改为 `dirnames[:] = sorted(keep)`——
   不改变任何判定语义，只把遍历变成确定序（`private < public` ⇒ 先撞拒绝、落库前中断），
   「拒绝时留下部分写入」不再被平台的 readdir 顺序随机暴露。
2. **守卫**（防回退）：`test_issue452` 新增 **C05** 源码锚点——
   `dirnames[:] = sorted(keep)` 必须在位，否则 Linux 乱序会让 A3 再次偶发红。
3. **诊断面**（这次白查一轮的直接原因）：`scripts/run_tests.py` 失败时只打 `tail` 的**末 6 行**，
   而 `tail` 本身只有末 **800** 字符——两层截断把**前部**的 `FAIL <项>` 行双双吞掉，
   CI 日志只剩「1 失败」看不到是哪条（本次只能看到 C 组 PASS）。
   现改为：`tail` 扩到末 **4000** 字符 + 失败时**优先打印含 `FAIL`/`ANCHOR-MISS` 的行**，再附末 6 行上下文。

# 病象（发版验证时实测，未发布即发现）

从 tag `v0.9.15` 建干净 worktree 跑完整发布链（`npm ci` → `npm run build` → `npm pack`），
包里**缺两件关键产物**：

```
package/lib/client.js            ✗   ← exports["./client"] 指向它
package/lib/lib/console_web.mjs  ✗
```

而 `build` 刚跑完时两件都在（`build_ui` 报「写入 9」）。装上这样的包，`dsh.client` 加载失败 ⇒
**UI 侧栏直接不出现**，且报错远离原因。

# 根因

`package.json` 的 `prepare` 脚本：

```json
"prepare": "node -e \"…fs.rmSync('lib',{recursive:true,force:true}); …tsc…\""
```

- 它会 `rmSync('lib')` 再跑 `tsc`，但**不含 `build_ui`**；
- 而 **`npm pack` 会触发 `prepare`** ⇒ 打包瞬间 `lib/` 被 tsc 重建，`build_ui` 先前写入的
  `lib/client.js` 与 `lib/lib/console_web.mjs` 被一并删掉。

时序：`npm ci`（prepare 建 lib）→ `npm run build`（rmSync + tsc + **build_ui 写 2 件**）
→ `npm pack`（**prepare 再 rmSync + tsc** ⇒ 那 2 件消失）→ 打包完成，缺件。

# 修法

1. **`prepare` 末尾追加 `&& python scripts/build_ui.py`**：让「凡会重建 `lib/` 的钩子」
   都一并补齐 UI 产物（`build` 早已串联，`prepare` 漏了）；
2. **`check_publish_artifact.py` 新增 R8（正向判据）**：`exports` / `files` 里**声明**的产物
   必须真在包里：
   - `exports["./client"] → lib/client.js`
   - `files` 含 `lib` ⇒ 包内须有 `lib/index.js`；含 `web` ⇒ 须有 `web/index.html`；含 `ui` ⇒ 须有 `ui/minimal/install.ps1`。

   背景：R1~R7 全是**负向**判据（「清单里不该有的东西」），缺一条正向判据——本次 R4 全程绿，
   因为 `lib`/`web` 确实在 `files` 里，只是**文件本身不在包里**。

CI 红（PR #693 · run-tests）：`FAIL scripts.test_check_publish_artifact_coverage`
（25 passed / 2 failed，明细为 L3 反向腿的两条）。

# 根因（两层）

1. **夹具不自洽**：该测试的「干净仓」夹具是
   `files: ["lib"]` + 只放 `lib/keep.txt`——**没有 `lib/index.js`**。
   这不是 R8 误伤：它就是「声明了 `lib` 却没给 `lib/index.js`」的形态，R8 判红**是对的**。
   修法：夹具补 `lib/index.js`，让「干净仓」真的干净（符合该腿的意图：新判据不误伤发版链路）。

2. **诊断面漏形态**：上一轮给 `run_tests.py` 加「失败时优先打印 `FAIL` 行」时只认了
   `FAIL ` / `ANCHOR-MISS` 两种前缀，而这批自检脚本的明细行是 **`[FAIL] <项>`**（带方括号）⇒
   两条真红在 CI 日志里仍然看不到（只显示 `25 passed, 2 failed`）。
   修法：过滤器追加 `[FAIL]` 前缀。

# 验证

| 项 | 读数 |
|---|---|
| `scripts/test_check_publish_artifact_coverage.py` | **27 passed / 0 failed**，rc=0（修前 25/2，rc=1） |
| R8 语义未被削弱 | 夹具补文件后该腿转绿；此前 `[FAIL] R8 … files 含 lib → lib/index.js` 的判别力仍然保留 |

# 说明

这是 R8 上线后的**第一次真实反馈**——它立刻抓出一个「声明与产物不一致」的既有夹具，
正是它设计要防的形态。夹具修好后反向腿恢复绿，说明 R8 不误伤发版链路。

# 裁定（使用者原话）

> 「这是一个权衡，希望快速反馈的人不希望重复改，希望稳定靠谱的人不希望轻易下决定。
> 这其中需要有一个价值观判断。**把选择权交给用户**。快，问题放一边。慢，细究根本原因。
> 模块化是一条通用的取舍方案。意思是**只做自己一个明确功能的修改**。
> **更高层的功能选型，是否开启交给上层**。」

# 落地（严格照这条判据分工）

| 层 | 职责 | 本次是否改 |
|---|---|---|
| **守卫**（md_cg/test_*，730 处 `--mutate`） | 只做自己那**一个**明确功能的检查；仍只认自己的 `--mutate`，**不自行判断该不该跑重质检** | **一行未改** |
| **上层**（`run_tests.py` / CI） | 决定「这次要不要跑重质检」 | **新增档位与入口** |

## 新增能力

```bash
python scripts/run_tests.py md_cg --gate fast      # 快速反馈：跳过重质检，逐条 SKIP 留痕
python scripts/run_tests.py md_cg --gate strict    # 缺省：全跑（不改变既有行为）
python scripts/run_tests.py md_cg --module test_issue452   # 按模块前缀过滤
```

| 设计点 | 取值 | 理由 |
|---|---|---|
| 缺省档位 | **strict** | 升级不降低既有门禁强度（「稳定靠谱的人」不会被动变更） |
| `fast` 的行为 | 跳过「重质检」守卫，**逐条打印 `SKIP … gate=fast：<原因>；要跑请用 --gate strict`** | 「快=问题放一边」但**不能变成静默跳过** |
| 重质检判据 | ①`HEAVY_GUARDS`（实测耗时：镜像复制全树 / 并发写数百条 / 3D 全量重算）②**复用** `check_guard_coverage.MUTATE_GUARDS`（定点变异自证登记表） | 两处数据源，避免与既有登记表漂移 |
| **防误用** | **CI 环境 + `fast` ⇒ 自动升级为 strict 并告警** | 「是否开启交给上层」——CI 就是上层；不允许本地捷径污染门禁 |
| 命名归一 | targets 是点号（`md_cg.test_x`）、登记表是斜杠（`md_cg/test_x`）⇒ 判据内归一 | 首版就踩了这个坑（fast 档当时「本批无重质检项」） |

# 验证

新增守卫 `scripts/test_run_tests_gate.py` **17 通过 / 0 失败**：

| 组 | 断言 |
|---|---|
| A | 判据归一（点号/斜杠都命中）、轻量同族不被误判、**复用 MUTATE_GUARDS 不另立清单** |
| B | fast 档 `SKIP … gate=fast` 留痕 + 跳过计数 + 轻量守卫照常执行 + 退出码 0 |
| C | strict 档不跳过、**真的跑了**重质检守卫、退出码 0 |
| D | `CI=true` + fast ⇒ 打印「自动升级为 strict」且不跳过（**CI 不会漏检**） |
| E | `--module test_issue452` 只列 2 条、计数正确 |
| F | 缺省仍是 strict、两个新参数在位 |

# 没做（如实）

- **`--max-mutations N`**：要真正生效必须在 730 处守卫里改判据，与「守卫只做自己那一个功能」冲突；
  若将来要做，正解是让守卫读**上层注入的 env**（如 `MDCG_MAX_MUTATIONS`）而不是各自解析参数；
- 未改任何守卫的重质检行为：`--gate fast` 只影响「跑不跑」，不影响「怎么跑」。

# 病象（#699，imFelixYang 在 DSH 0.2.1-rc.3 实测）

`/lingshu`、`/plugins/lingshu/*`（**连静态资源**）全部 `503 {"error":"宿主鉴权不可用"}`；
同一宿主进程内 `/` 给 401、另一插件路由给 403 ⇒ 只有 `/lingshu` 恒 503，侧边栏入口还在、点开空白。

# 根因（两层，本 commit 修第一层）

```js
// console_web.mjs 原实现
export function createConsoleHandler(mdcg, config, assets, connection) {
  ...
  if (!connection || typeof connection.admit !== 'function') return reply(res, 503, {...})
}
// 挂载点（库内 installConsoleWeb）
const handler = createConsoleHandler(mdcg, config, assets, ctx.get('connection'))   // ← 只取一次
```

cordis 的 `Context.get(name, strict = true)` 在服务 fiber **未就绪时返回 `undefined`**；
挂载瞬间拿不到就把 `undefined` **永久闭包**进 handler ⇒ 此后每个请求都命中 503，宿主就绪也不自愈。

> 第二层（`src/index.ts` 的 `inject = ['tools']` 不含 `connection`，故无就绪保证）**未在本 commit 处理**：
> 改成实时取之后，即使注入顺序变也能自愈；是否把 `connection` 加入 `inject` 属另一决策（会改变 `apply` 的启动依赖面），留待评估。

# 改动

|---|---|
| `payload/src/lib/console_web.mjs` · `payload/lib/lib/console_web.mjs` | 第 4 参 `connection` → **`getConnection`（取值函数）**；handler 内 `const connection = connectionOf()` **每次请求实时取**；`typeof getConnection === 'function' ? getConnection : () => getConnection` 保证**旧调用方式（传值）行为不变** |
| 同上 | 503 文案 `宿主鉴权不可用` → **`宿主鉴权服务尚未就绪，请稍后重试`**（避免让用户误判为永久损坏） |

# 这不是"又发现一个 bug"，是**我上一个 PR 自己的锅**

`--module` 是本轮 #696 加的。它的 help 文本我写的是：

```
--module MODULE   按模块名前缀过滤（如 md_cg/test_issue4 或 test_issue4）
```

**教的是斜杠写法**，而实现是 `n.startswith(args.module) or args.module in n` ——**没有归一化**。
于是照着文档写的选择器**选中零个目标**，而入口仍然：

```
SUMMARY 0/0 通过，0 跳过（依赖缺失/平台不符）
rc=0
```

## 为什么这比「测试失败」危险（1_ai 会话的定档理由，我认同）

| 形态 | 现象 | 危险度 |
|---|---|---|
| 真失败 | 有 FAIL 行 + rc≠0 | 会喊 |
| 确定性跳过 | 有 SKIP + 计数 + 理由 | 会留下痕迹 |
| **零选中** | **`SUMMARY 0/0` + rc=0** | **只会沉默地说"通过"**——CI 只看退出码时，整条流水线的绿都可能是假的 |

复现（1_ai 会话给的对照实验，我在本机复验一致）：

| 选择器 | 修前列出 | 修前执行 |
|---|---|---|
| `test_probe` | 1 个 | rc=1 |
| `md_cg.test_probe` | 1 个 | rc=1 |
| **`md_cg/test_probe`** | **0 个** | **rc=0** ← 假绿 |

# 修法（两处，缺一不成立）

1. **归一化**：新增 `_module_match(selector, name)` —— 斜杠与点号等价（`md_cg/test_x` ≡ `md_cg.test_x`）、忽略 `.py` 后缀、空选择器**不命中**（不是"全选"）；
2. **零选中不得返回 0**：执行路径 `return 2` 并打印「无匹配目标：group=… -k=… --module=… —— 拒绝以 0/0「通过」收场」+ 提示模块名是点号形态；`--list` 保持 0（查看语义）但仍打印原因。

feat(rust): F26-25 Rust 侧重音折叠对齐 Python——零依赖下的 963 条映射表 + 跨实现守卫

# 病灶（#659 F26-25）

`rust/src/text.rs::normalize_en` 原先把「非 ASCII 且非中文」的字符**一律变空格**：

```
café  ->  caf     ← Rust
café  ->  cafe    ← Python `fold_accents`（NFKC → NFD → 剥组合记号 → NFC）
```

⇒ 两侧互不可命中。而 `rust/Cargo.toml` 明写「**零第三方依赖**：与 md_cg 的 D-005 约束一致，
且无需联网取 crate」⇒ 用不了 `unicode-normalization`，只能内置表。

# 路线：按 Python 口径**生成**表，而不是手抄

| 步 | 做法 |
|---|---|
| 1 | 枚举 Unicode，取「NFKC → NFD → 剥 **三区间** Mn（U+0300–036F / U+1AB0–1AFF / U+1DC0–1DFF）→ NFC 后仍为**单字符**且与原字符不同」的字符 |
| 2 | 生成 `rust/src/text_fold.rs`：`LATIN_FOLD: [(char, char); 963]` + `fold_accents()`（表查找 + 记号剥离） |
| 3 | `normalize_en` 开头先折叠，再走原有字符过滤 |

**为什么单字符这个条件很重要**：它自动排除 `ﬁ`→`fi` 这类多字符兼容分解，让 Rust 的
`char → char` 表与 Python 的 `str → str` 语义在可表范围内等价。

# 两个我踩到并被守卫抓住的坑（都写进注释了）

**坑① 漏了 NFKC**：初版表只用 `NFD → 剥 Mn → NFC`，于是 `ẛ`(U+1E9B) 折成 `ſ`(U+017F)，
而 Python 先做 NFKC 会得 `s`。跨实现守卫 **B1 精准报出 `[(ẛ, ſ, s)]`** ⇒ 补 NFKC 后表从 497 条扩到 963 条（NFKC 补入 465 条）。

**坑② 初版只收拉丁四区**：我当时的文档写着「希腊/西里尔未收」，但 Python **会**折希腊（39 个）。
于是「Rust 不折、Python 折」构成**新分叉**——守卫 **G2** 抓出。修正为「按 Python 能折的全部生成」，
并改掉那段过时的边界声明。这两条正好印证模块头一开始写的「扩表前先加跨实现守卫样例」。

# 验证

| 项 | 读数 |
|---|---|
| `cargo test`（rust/） | **42 passed / 0 failed**（含 7 条 fold 单测：折叠/不折 ß·ø/不折日文浊点/剥组合记号/表有序/端到端 `normalize_en("café") == "cafe"`） |
| `scripts/test_rust_fold_parity.py` | **29 通过 / 0 失败** |
| `python -m md_cg.test_issue644_637_636`（#636 守卫） | rc=0 |
| `python scripts/gate_rust_crate_test.py`（R-7 腿①） | **PASS：42 passed / 0 failed** |

跨实现守卫生效面（逐条核）：

| 组 | 断言 |
|---|---|
| A | 表可解析、声明条目数 == 实际条目数、量级断言 |
| **B** | **逐条**核对 963 条 `ch -> base` 与 Python `fold_accents(ch)` 一致（就是这条抓出坑①） |
| C | 表严格有序且无重复（Rust `binary_search` 依赖） |
| D | `ß`/`ø`/`Ø`/`Æ` **不得**入表（无规范分解，Python 也不变） |
| E | 日文浊点 `が/ガ/ぱ/ば` **不得**入表且 Python 也不折（F26-27 的边界） |
| F | 典型词两侧同向：`café→cafe` `CAFÉ→CAFE` `señor→senor` `Über→Uber` `Ångström→Angstrom` `straße→straße` |
| G | 希腊重音**已全部入表**（覆盖而非"假装不覆盖"） |

# 已知边界（如实）

- 本实现是**近似路线**（预组合表 + 记号剥离），不是真 NFKC/NFD/NFC；对表内字符等价，表外走原样；
- 表覆盖「Python 能折的单字符映射」；Python 能折成**多字符**的（如 `ﬁ`→`fi`）两侧都不折（Rust 不收，Python 的 `len==1` 条件也不收）；
- 未改 Python 侧任何代码——本次只让 Rust 追上 Python。

fix(dsh): authenticate memory web routes (#822)

The five MemSearch Web UI routes currently bypass DSH's login and request-origin checks. Route every request through the host connection service before reading memory or executing actions, and return 503 while that service is unavailable. Authentication is resolved per request because the service mounts after the plugin.

Reproduced on a real isolated DSH 0.2.1-rc.2 instance: the unauthenticated home page returned 401 while the plugin returned test memory. After the fix, all five routes reject unauthenticated requests with 401 and cross-origin requests with 403, including requests carrying a valid login cookie. Authenticated Chromium access works both directly and through a TCP port forward. Existing route tests cover authenticated actions and path protections; new tests cover rejection before side effects and late service availability.

feat(config-schema): accept the codebuddy harness key (#6436)

Add `codebuddy` to HARNESS_KEYS so a `plugin.codebuddy` section in ov.conf
resolves to a real harness override instead of being reported as a typo.
This is the shared-library half of the CodeBuddy Code integration; the host
adapter that consumes it lands separately in agent-hook-plugin.

The shared library reaches every registered plugin, so all six take a patch
bump as the version gate requires.

feat(agent-hook-plugin): add the CodeBuddy Code CLI as a host adapter (#5860)

* feat(agent-hook-plugin): add the CodeBuddy Code host adapter

CodeBuddy matches Claude Code on event names and the output envelope, so
the adapter is a stages map plus an envelope, following the KimiCode
precedent: hosts/codebuddy.mjs owns the event mapping, the deny-only
guard (this host has no advisory channel under PreToolUse), the
is_internal_continuation prompt gate, and the capture/commit policy;
hosts/codebuddy-turns.mjs decodes CodeBuddy's JSONL transcript — where
tool calls are separate records and the human ask is wrapped in
host-injected markup — into the incremental turns the dispatcher sends.

The host contract the adapter was measured against moves in as
hosts/codebuddy/DESIGN.md, with a new section recording the adapter
mapping and the v1 scope: no subagent capture (the dispatcher has no
subagent stage), no resume/compact archive injection, and no hard-coded
compressor defaults. The three skills ship with the plugin.

* test(agent-hook-plugin): cover the CodeBuddy adapter and its decoder

The decoder cases are the ones real transcripts taught us: host blocks
around the ask, a quoted earlier turn that must not be mistaken for the
current one, host-authored records that carry no human text, and tool
calls that are separate records from the messages they belong to — plus
the incremental cursor and a parity test against the server-side
workbuddy adapter's block-tag list. The adapter cases drive the guard,
the continuation gate, the envelopes, the commit policy, and the capture
path through the real hook entry against a mock OpenViking, including
the idempotent cursor and the offline queue.

`--harness codebuddy` assembles a self-contained plugin under
~/.openviking/agent-integrations/codebuddy/marketplace/openviking-memory
— the shared runtime beside the adapters, because CodeBuddy installs
the plugin directory wholesale into its cache — registers it as a local
marketplace, and installs it through the host CLI. Detection, selection,
validation, uninstall, and the printed next steps follow the KimiCode
path. The uninstall also removes the host's cached copy, which the CLI
leaves behind.

08-community-plugins.md in both languages rather than as a numbered page
of its own: the host's hook feature is still Beta and recall runs only
in the TUI, so the community section sets the right expectations. The
overview reaches it through the existing ZCode / AstrBot row, and the
{harness} enum in the client configuration reference gains `codebuddy`.

The plugin changed, so every host-facing manifest takes a patch bump as
the version gate requires, and the CodeBuddy manifest joins the PAIRED
list: the host and the local marketplace both resolve an installed
plugin by the manifest version.

* test(installer): name the codebuddy toggle in the TUI selection test

The test sets every harness toggle explicitly before tui_finish_selection;
the new codebuddy entry has to be named too, or the unset variable fails
the comparison under `set -e`.

* fix(installer): restore the comment marker the codebuddy header line lost

The `codebuddy` line in the header's harness table was written without its
leading `#`, so every run of the script executed it as a command —
`codebuddy a local marketplace registered with codebuddy, installed from
~/.codebuddy/plugins` — starting a stray host session with the comment text
as its prompt. That is what stalled the test glob once: the TUI test feeds
the prelude to bash over stdin, the line ran, and the spawned session held
the runner's output pipe open.

While here, the two things that line's neighbours exposed: the top-level
toggle defaults need `SEL_CODEBUDDY` (and `SEL_KIMICODE`, which the reset
block already had) or `set -u` trips on the unset variable, and the TUI's
selectable count has to grow with the new item or the codebuddy entry is
never enumerated.

* chore(plugins): bump agent-hook-plugin to 0.5.25 for the CodeBuddy host

The CodeBuddy adapter changes the distributed plugin on top of the 0.5.24
release that added codebuddy to the harness keys, so every paired
host-facing manifest takes the next patch version.

* fix(agent-hook-plugin): attribute CodeBuddy tool use before any reply to the assistant

A tool call the model makes before writing text followed the user
message in the transcript and was folded into the user turn, so it was
captured with role user. Tool records now open an assistant turn unless
they follow an assistant message. Also drops an unused re-export.

* chore(plugins): register the CodeBuddy skill copies with the shared sync

The three skills under hosts/codebuddy/skills were committed but not
listed in SKILL_TARGETS, so sync never refreshed them and its drift
checks did not cover them.

* refactor(agent-hook-plugin): drop the CodeBuddy keyword capture gate

No other agent-hook host reads captureMode, and the trigger list only
held batches back. CodeBuddy now sends every captured batch like the
other hosts.

* docs: drop the CodeBuddy doctor advice

ov-memory-doctor.mjs has no codebuddy client and falls back to Cursor,
so pointing CodeBuddy users at it reports the wrong host.

* docs: describe the CodeBuddy commit policy the adapter implements

The capability reference claimed a 20,000-token threshold, a synchronous
PreCompact commit and a commit at the next start. The adapter commits
every commitTurnThreshold captured messages like Kimi Code, runs capture
detached, and SessionStart only replays queued writes.

* chore(plugins): publish a codebuddy release channel

The installer resolves each harness through channels.json, but the
release and docs-download generators hard-code their harness lists and
left codebuddy out, so a release-pinned CodeBuddy install had no entry.

* fix(installer): keep CodeBuddy plugin files until the host uninstalls it

Uninstall removed the plugin cache and marketplace even when the
codebuddy CLI was missing or its uninstall failed, leaving an enabled
plugin whose hooks point at deleted files. Now the files go only after
the CLI uninstall succeeds; otherwise the installer prints the commands.
The assembled plugin also no longer carries a stale hosts/codebuddy copy.

* docs(agent-hook-plugin): list CodeBuddy Code among the supported hosts

The package description and READMEs still named only the earlier hosts.

* fix(installer): clean up a CodeBuddy plugin the host never installed

The uninstall kept every file whenever `codebuddy plugin uninstall`
failed, which it always does when install registered the marketplace
but could not install the plugin. That left a marketplace and files no
uninstall run could remove. A plugin missing from `codebuddy plugin list`
now counts as gone. The manual fallback commands are separated with `;`
so a failing first step no longer blocks the rest.

* fix(installer): stay quiet when there is no CodeBuddy install to remove

A detected ~/.codebuddy with no CLI and no OpenViking files means nothing was installed, so the keep-the-files warning was noise. Also tidy a decoder comment the role fix left stale.

* docs: fix the CodeBuddy notes anchor and placement

The zh link used the English anchor, which breaks the built-anchor check, and the section sat between the legacy custom-integration anchors and their heading. Move it next to Kimi Code in both languages.

fix(queue): stop deduplicating the retries that run before a lease exists (#6197)

The memory-parent window (45s, #769) is skipped for retries that hold a lease:
_enqueue_semantic_retry already calls enqueue(..., deduplicate_memory=False) and
raises if the queue still answers 'deduplicated'.

The retries that run before a lease is acquired do not. breaker.check() happens
before work.acquire_lock(), so an open circuit breaker re-enqueues through
SemanticMessageWork.reenqueue's no-lock branch, which called
queue.enqueue(msg) with deduplication on. If the message was first queued less
than 45s earlier, the retry was replaced by 'deduplicated', the caller still
returned ProcessResult.requeued(), and the worker ACKed the only delivery -
the work was lost with no error and no replacement.

SkillSemanticMessageWork.reenqueue has the same shape.

Pass deduplicate_memory=False in both no-lock branches, reusing the flag the
lock-owning path introduced rather than adding a second mechanism.

Reachable for memory-context messages without a coalesce_key (utils/summarizer.py
derives context_type from the URI), and for a stale message downgraded to
file-only work, since that path clears coalesce_key before retrying.

Does not add retry bounding or backoff; that stays with #4451.

fix(plugins): read profile and memory listings from peer scope (#5246)

* fix(plugins): read profile and memory listings from peer scope

SessionStart profile injection read `viking://user/<space>/memories/...`
unconditionally, while capture has written to
`viking://user/<space>/peers/<id>/memories/...` since the user/peer memory
isolation model landed. The reader and the writer therefore never agreed on a
path: `<user-profile>` was empty for every repository workspace, whatever was
in the peer profile.

`actorPeerId` was already accepted by `buildProfileBlock` and already passed by
its caller, but it only becomes the `X-OpenViking-Actor-Peer` request header.
That header is a view filter, not a path rewrite, so it could not redirect the
hardcoded URIs.

Resolve each category independently, peer scope first, user scope as fallback:

    const roots = [];
    if (actorPeerId) roots.push(`.../peers/${actorPeerId}/memories`);
    roots.push(`.../memories`);

Per category rather than per scope, because a peer that has `preferences/` or
`entities/` but no `profile.md` would otherwise win the scope and drop the user
profile from the block entirely - a state that occurs in practice, not just in
theory. That case is covered by a test.

Request cost is unchanged in the common case (5 calls), 6 when a peer has
listings but no profile, and 8 when the peer is absent entirely, which
reproduces the previous `null` result exactly.

Also fixes the test that should have caught this. Its mock answered
`content/read` with the same body for any URI and asserted the user-scope URI,
so it encoded the bug as expected behavior. The mock now serves a distinct body
per scope and the peer-routing test asserts the peer body is present and the
user body is absent.

New unit coverage in `profile-inject.test.mjs` drives `buildProfileBlock`
against a scope-aware fetch double and asserts which scope supplied each
category.

Vendored copies regenerated with `examples/memory-plugin-shared/sync.mjs`.

* fix(retain): don't checkpoint a document as committed while a retain session may still buffer it (#6099)

The streaming retain wrote the facts_committed_document_ids checkpoint as soon as a
document's facts were handed to the store. A store whose RetainSession buffers until
commit() had not made them durable yet, so when another document failed and the

for the whole retain, so there is nothing to resume from. The SQL path is unchanged.

feat(decision-model): count the request ceiling and recall's caps in the model's own vocabulary (#6115)

* feat(decision-model): count the request ceiling and recall's caps in the model's own vocabulary

The decision model's request ceiling and the reranker's per-memory and query
caps were counted in HINDSIGHT_API_TOKENIZER_ENCODING (o200k_base by default),
while the endpoint counts its window with the served model's tokenizer. On
mixed-script text the two diverge widely, so a request sized to fit could still
overflow, and a capped memory could still run past its cap.

HINDSIGHT_API_DECISION_MODEL_TOKENIZER names the vocabulary. It defaults to
'jev' for the typesafe provider (toktok's estimate of Jev's count) and to the
configured encoding for the others; set it when an endpoint serves another
model (e.g. qwen3.5). token_encoding gains an encoding argument on
truncate_to_tokens and accepts 'jev', which has no ids and so only goes
through toktok's batch count / truncate.
