feat(recall): prune flag for the decision-model reranker (#6131)

* recall: prune flag for the decision-model reranker

HINDSIGHT_API_RECALL_DECISION_MODEL_PRUNE (off by default): with a decision
model set up for recall, it can also drop candidates instead of only ordering
them — one judged no help (below 0.2, or below 40% of the best, reusing the
ranking answer), or one that repeats a better-ranked candidate (one pairwise
question, asked only of same-date pairs that share enough words, among the 40
best). The best candidate always survives.

* refactor(recall): pruning lives in decision_rerank_interface

So a service outside hindsight-api that loads the interface prunes exactly as
recall does. The interface builds pruning's questions and decides what is
dropped; the reranker only sends them:
- DecisionRerank.relevant: the no-help cut (below 0.2, or below 40% of the best).
- DecisionRerank.repeat_questions: the repeat pairs worth asking (RepeatQuestion,
  each with its own state), behind the date and word-overlap guards.
- DecisionRerank.pruned: the scores with every dropped candidate at 0.0.
The tuning constants and their bench notes move with it. Behaviour is unchanged:
TestPrune and test_73 pass as they were.

* recall prune: ask the repeat question only within one fact type

An observation is built from the very facts it repeats, and choosing between them
is prefer_observations, which keeps the observation. Asked as a repeat, the
observation ranked below its raw fact was dropped, so a recall preferring
observations got the raw fact and no observation (recall eval
observations/prefer-observations, with pruning on). The reranker now receives
each candidate's fact type (rerank_fact_types, set beside rerank_shared_context)
and DecisionRerank.repeat_questions skips pairs of different types.

* recall prune: ask the repeat questions in the same round trip as the keep ones

The repeat pairs are now picked from the caller's order before any keep answer and
sent alongside the keep request, so pruning adds no second round trip. Each pair is
asked both ways round, since the model's answer is not symmetric and the rank order
that decides which one is Memory A is only known afterwards.

Folding the repeat check into the keep question was tried on the prune bench and
dropped: similar memories listed in the question caught 3 of 52 repeats, and the
whole pool in the state lost 8 of 76 needed facts.

* recall prune: drop only what is judged no help, not repeats

The repeat check is removed. It needs both memories in one question, which a
single request over a 250-candidate pool cannot pick pairs for without a second
round trip or hundreds of requests; asked with the pool in the state it lost
needed facts. The no-help cut reuses the ranking answers, so pruning costs no
extra request.

- interface: DecisionRerank.pruned(answers) replaces relevant/repeat_questions/pruned
- reranker: no repeat requests, no fact-type context var
- system stub: repeat rule removed; test_73 expects both copies back
- recall evals: duplicates come back with pruning too; pools no longer assert one copy
- docs and env templates describe the cut only

fix(worker): shutdown no longer waits out a long maintenance job (#6092)

* fix(worker): shutdown no longer waits out a long maintenance job

A worker's graceful shutdown closes the engine, and close() stops the
maintenance loop by awaiting the job in progress. A scheduled mental-model
refresh pass checks every due model in turn, and with thousands of models
due a pass can run for tens of minutes. A shutdown that lands mid-pass then
waits until the platform kills the process at the end of its termination
grace period, so a rolling restart of N workers can take N grace periods.

- MaintenanceLoop.stop() lets the job in progress reach a stopping point for
  a few seconds, then cancels it. Each unit of work is its own transaction,
  and whatever was not reached is still due on the next tick.
- The scheduled-refresh pass and the consolidation reconcile check for stop
  between items, so they usually end on their own within that grace.
- The worker bounds the engine's close() at 60s, so no other close step can
  hold a shutdown for a whole grace period either.

Tests: a job that never reaches a stopping point is cancelled, a cooperative
one finishes on its own, a job failing while stopping does not raise, a
refresh pass stops after the model in progress, and a hanging close() is
abandoned at the bound. The stop and pass tests fail without the fix.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_011Fo4NboRJPywxb1UfwpneJ

* fix(worker): bound the wait for a cancel to land, and backstop the exit

Review follow-up. Cancelling a task and then awaiting it waits as long as the
task takes to accept the cancel, unbounded: a job or close() that catches
CancelledError, or makes a call that does not yield, held shutdown anyway.
asyncio.wait_for has the same shape (it cancels at the timeout, then waits).

- MaintenanceLoop.stop(): after cancelling, wait a bounded few seconds for the
  job to finish; past that, log and leave it behind instead of awaiting it.
- The worker's engine close: asyncio.wait instead of wait_for, with the same
  bounded wait after the cancel.
- A daemon timer armed on the first shutdown signal exits the process if it is
  still running 120s later. It covers what no bound inside the loop can, such as
  asyncio.run's own teardown, which waits on every task left. In-flight tasks
  are returned to 'pending' before any of this, so nothing is lost.

Tests: a maintenance job and a close() that each swallow the cancel and stay
pending (stop() and the close return within the bounds; on the previous code the
close test fails and the run then hangs in teardown), and the backstop fires,
or does nothing once cancelled.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_011Fo4NboRJPywxb1UfwpneJ

fix(remote-bridge): announce a turn end once the session is quiet

A turn/end increment ends one turn, not the work the session still holds:
the child sessions it delegated to and the jobs the host keeps under them
outlive it. Both turn-end surfaces now wait for the host's own answer that
nothing is left running, so the notification and the lock-screen card agree
with the client's SessionRun instead of claiming the work finished.

The wait is bounded at 600 s (DSH_REMOTE_BRIDGE_TURN_END_QUIET_MAX_MS),
cleared on dispose, and books the rate windows at the real send. A new turn
the bridge can see starting drops the held end.

fix(remote-bridge): read a new turn only from increments that prove one

Any increment that was not a turn end counted as "a turn started", which the
follow stream does not support: a child's settle notice arrives on the parent as
a user message with an agent actor, and usage counts and catalog changes arrive
at the end of a turn. A turn ending while its child still ran therefore had its
held announcement dropped the moment that child settled, which is the case the
quiet gate exists for.

isTurnStartDelta now names the evidence once, for the connection drain and the
standing watchers alike: streaming assistant work, and a user message this
session's own user wrote. The watcher note's reporting bullet states the
shipped ordering and log line again.

fix(remote-bridge): deliver an event once per APNs token, not once per row

One iPhone held the same APNs token on two roster rows and got two identical
notifications: pair.finish enrolls on every accept, enroll minted a row per
accept instead of reusing the one its fingerprint already owned, registerPush
only wrote the connected device's row, and #announce admitted the event once by
(sessionId, event) and then sent it once per target.

The sender now converges its targets by deviceToken before fan-out, enroll
reuses the row a fingerprint already has and moves only the credential, and a
load compacts the table to one row per fingerprint and one registration per
token, writing the result back through the roster's serialized queue. The
schema stays version 2, no frame, capability or topic changes, and the three
existing push limits keep their values.

fix(market): retry a throttled Cloudflare API in the deploy lane

The Deploy Market lane failed three times on dev (runs 40350674320,
40367640238, 40430514377) about a second into scripts/deploy-market:
wrangler's first request, GET /accounts/{account}/workers/services/
dsh-market, came back 429 Too Many Requests with no Retry-After header,
and wrangler only backs off when that header is present, so the deploy
died on the first throttled response.

Every wrangler invocation now runs under a bounded retry policy:
MAX_ATTEMPTS = 4 with 5s / 20s / 60s between them. Only transient
conditions are retried - HTTP 429, HTTP 5xx in the shapes wrangler
prints, "malformed response from the API", and socket-level errors -
while a bad config, a rejected token, a missing binding or a
non-transient D1 error keeps the old fail-fast path and the byte
identical message. When the budget is spent the failure carries the
reason, the attempt count, the Cloudflare Ray ID and a bounded tail of
the captured output, and the child's output still reaches the job log
as it happens.

The lane's other gates are unchanged: the market-build preflight, the
D1 migration step, the TURNSTILE_SECRET and ASSET_ATTEST_SECRET
fail-closed checks, the siteverify pairing probe and every exit code.
scripts/deploy-market.test.mjs drives the policy through injected
attempts and waits (no sleeping, no network) plus two real-child cases
for the output relay and the stdin payload.

fix(liangshen): page tool_activate from the catalog's published partition

Under the default `ptc` presentation the catalog installs
`agent.ctx.tools.restrict({deny})` before the request assembles, so the paged
families are already gone from every scoped reader. `tool_activate` recomputed
the page from `agent.ctx.tools.schemas(agent)` and therefore found an empty
page ("paged namespaces in this session: (none)") while the same request's
catalog advertised those namespaces — every MCP namespace was unreachable in
production, and the native presentation was the only path that worked because
no restriction is installed there.

Publish the pre-restriction partition from the paging sync and read it back in
the activation tool, so the catalog message and the tool that loads a namespace
come from one fact. The schema read stays as the fallback for scopes nothing
pages: native presentation, a deployment without the catalog row, or a test
stub.

feat(task-board): clear labels whose tasks have all settled

The label manager could rename and delete one label at a time, so a label kept
alive by an old experiment stayed in the filter row until someone hunted it down
row by row. Cleanup adds a threshold (5 by default, 1..99) and judges the whole
ledger: a label is a candidate when fewer tasks than that carry it and every one
of them is done or failed. Archived cards are counted on the same terms, so a
card that is archived and still unfinished holds its label back.

Candidates are computed before anything is written: with none the row only says
so and leaves the ledger alone, and with some it asks for confirmation listing
each label with the number of tasks carrying it. Each accepted label then leaves
through the existing delete-tag ledger transition, so cleanup adds no wire action
and no second write path.

The label-management decision record owns the rule and records the two rejected
shapes (a batch wire action, an automatic sweep); the task-tags note's "no
cleanup entry" line was stale and now points at the manager.

feat(task-board): carry the label clear rule on a corner question mark

The clear control acts on the whole ledger, so trailing the label list made it
read as the last row's action. It now sits in the card header beside the title,
and the rule it explains moves out of the body: a round `?` holds the sentence as
its native title (the convention every icon button here already uses) and as an
aria-describedby description kept visually hidden, so the corner stays two
controls wide while a pointer, a keyboard and a screen reader all still get the
rule. The "nothing matched" notice stays supporting text in the body, where a
status line belongs, rather than travelling with the control.

The corner cluster reuses the existing contracts — .scheduleZone for the labeled
threshold field, .ghostButton for the commit — and adds only the help button plus
the hidden-text utility. Assertions pin the new shape: the `?` carries the hint
as title and description, and both it and the commit live in the header.

docs(task-board): state what the corner question mark actually reaches

A native title renders on pointer hover only; the hidden description is what
covers assistive technology. The comment claimed keyboard parity it does not
have, and recorded why a styled tooltip was rejected (the modal clips overflow).

fix(dsh-agents): run an unbound squad in the Host default directory

The workspace registry was read once while the row applied, but the official
registry's Service.init is asynchronous and finishes afterwards, so the face
stayed undefined for the life of the process. Both halves then failed: the state
view offered no workspace to pick (the form degraded to a typed id) and every
run that pinned one answered workspace-unavailable.

- make the pin optional: an unbound squad opens its session with no workspaceId
  and the Host composes it in its own default directory; a pin that is set still
  fails closed with workspace-unavailable or workspace-unknown
- drop the unreachable workspace-required code and its status mapping
- render the squad workspace as a picker even when no registry is reported, and
  keep a pin the registry does not list visible instead of silently clearing it
- realign the model-facing tool descriptions, both READMEs, the remote-bridge
  error-code enum and the Agent Note that owned the refusal list

feat(task-board): move the label manager's whole rule onto its question mark

The body kept a second explanation after the clear rule moved to the corner —

The original defect lived in the wiring, not in the service: a face captured

fix(liangshen): replay activations dispatched from inside a program

Under the ptc presentation the wire carries run_code alone, so tool_activate is
reached from inside a program and the harness records tool/ptc-dispatch — no
top-level tool/call is ever written. replayActivations read only tool/call, so
the active set was always empty: every activation reported success, the page
never lifted, the same namespace could be activated again for ever, and the MCP
families stayed unreachable no matter how many times the model asked for them.

Both event shapes now feed the same recency list in session order, and an errored
dispatch activates nothing, the same rule the tool/result pairing already used.
Proven against a real session log: replaying production events yields the activated
namespaces, while the same log with dispatch events removed yields none.

Unit cases cover a successful and an errored dispatch; an integration case drives
the whole loop — dispatch recorded, catalog replays it, scope stops withholding.

fix(dsh-agents): read the settled command record, not the handler result

The official dispatcher answers { commandId, result } for every settled command.
The permission pin read kind off that record, so result.kind was always
undefined and every successful switch was reported as "the permission command
failed" — which is why a squad member with a pinned permission could never be
launched, while a member without one ran fine.

The task board already unwraps the record this way; this brings the run gateway
to the same contract. The new cases pin all three outcomes: the success record,
a refused preset whose own text must survive, and a Host that acknowledges
nothing.

fix(storage): fork clone takes one CAS ref per cloned row, not per hash

session delete then over-released and drove the refcount negative, and
delete-on-zero GC swept bytes sessions still referenced — a fork could

fix: let Codex/opencode WebSocket delta continuations skip full-history reconstruction (#4804)

A previous_response_id continuation used to expand into the complete
reconstructed history before admission/processing: every turn re-materialized
all retained originals (O(N) JSON rebuild plus repeated serialization), and
once the reconstruction crossed the byte budget the turn was refused with 413
before ACP ever ran — stranding sessions whose model view had already been
compressed to <1 MiB. The client's actual wire frame was tens of KiB; the
cost was entirely bili's internal expansion.

The delta now rides the unified transcript:

- On an eligible continuation (matching checkpoint id, unified storage
  readable, all prior outputs echoable), the session dispatches the small
  body [prior outputs, new input] instead of the O(N) reconstruction and
  stamps the envelope with the commit-time identity signature of the
  dispatched body's last core message (non-enumerable symbol property).
- prepare-responses renders the outbound prefix from the server's own
  transcript rows (buildAnchoredView: same loader/anchor machinery as
  snapshot-render, no chain walk — the client vouches for the prefix by
  protocol) and appends the delta tail verbatim.
- The seam is verified against the stored row's identity signature; any
  mismatch (or missing store / non-echoable output / rollout off) falls back
  to the legacy full-reconstruction path, and an engine-side seam miss
  answers 400 previous_response_not_found — the client's standard recovery
  (full replay) re-anchors losslessly. Nothing is dropped: the store keeps
  every original.
- Checkpoints chain (base/tail/tailSig) so steady-state turns grow memory
  O(1); the legacy expand() walks the chain only on fallback.
- Echoing the prior outputs into the delta body also gets them ingested into
  the unified transcript (rows are request-side only), keeping the
  server-rendered prefix complete across restarts.

Behavior changes (disclosed):
- New rollout feature wsDeltaContinuation, DEFAULT OFF (0%): zero behavior
  change until ramped; force on via BILI_ROLLOUT_WS_DELTA_CONTINUATION=1 or
  rollout.features.wsDeltaContinuation.
- When ON and eligible: the upstream request for a delta turn carries the
  server-rendered folded prefix plus echoed outputs plus the tail instead of
  the client-resent full history (removes the internal O(N) materialization
  and its 413 window).
- A new 400 previous_response_not_found can be returned on a delta turn when
  the transcript seam cannot be verified; the client recovers with a full
  replay (no data loss).

Tests: tests/issue4804-ws-delta-anchor.test.ts (engine/history/session units,
both gate directions) and tests/issue4804-ws-delta-e2e.test.ts (real proxy +
fake WS upstream: delta keeps the conversation without resending it; unknown

fix(storage): quick_check no longer blocks boot on big stores (#4609)

PRAGMA quick_check walks every B-tree page of every table, so a 14 GB
index.db costs ~260 s of single-core scan on EVERY open — and because
open() runs it before listen, the native lane's 60 s spawn budget kills
the child mid-scan, the host falls back to direct (no compression) for
its whole lifetime, and every restart repeats the scan (#4609).

against) preserved wherever it is cheap:

- verdict cache: index.db.chk.json records the last outcome keyed by
  (schema version, index.db stat, -wal stat). An unchanged file set
  skips the rescan; any write or a schema upgrade invalidates the key; a
  hot -wal left by a killed process changes the key by construction —
  exactly the risky boots that deserve a rescan. A clean close of a
  verified store refreshes the key onto the post-checkpoint stats, so
  the normal restart path is rescan-free.

- size gate: stores at or below 512 MiB keep the synchronous
  pre-migration check (a couple of seconds at most). Larger stores check
  post-open on a second read-only connection in a worker thread (WAL
  allows concurrent readers; the main handle has already run recovery),
  so open() returns in milliseconds. A background failure is recorded
  loudly, cached, and makes the NEXT open throw StorageIntegrityError so
  the existing #4175 quarantine-and-reopen-fresh machinery runs.

fix(server): an unconditional 304 from the catalog endpoint is off-spec — no phantom hit

The catalog cache replayed its cached 200 on ANY 304 and extended
freshness by another maxAge. That is correct only when the request
was conditional (the end client sent if-none-match / if-modified-
since; the wrapper itself never sends a validator). A 304 answered
to an UNCONDITIONAL GET is off-spec — some transparent middleboxes
do it anyway — and treating it as a hit manufactured a phantom
success: six more hours of freshness, all real response headers
discarded, and the relay billing it as a genuine catalog fetch.

Gate the 304 branch on the request having carried a conditional
header; otherwise invalidate the cache and pass the odd response
through, same as any other unexpected status.

its name always implied; a new test pins the off-spec passthrough
plus cache invalidation.

fix: stream the MySQL v8 upgrade per-session under a cross-process lock (#4666 review)

Rework per PR #4678 review: the v8 data step no longer materializes the
whole messages x content join in memory before deleting rows. It now
mirrors the sqlite #4677 streaming design:

- one session per transaction, 500-row seq-cursor pages; memory holds one
  page window plus one session's keeper keys, never the stored bytes
  (closes the OOM class reported in #4806);
- dedup happens inside each session's ordered scan (first arrival kept),
  so duplicates whose two generations sit on different pages are still
  paired;
- a crash between sessions leaves done sessions committed; the stamp gate
  resumes on next boot without reprocessing them;
- rows whose content bytes are missing from the CAS get the printable
  absent marker (byte-parity with schema.ts) instead of rescanning forever;
- progress log every 100 sessions plus start/complete/failure guidance.

Concurrency (review item 3): the data step runs under a server-side named
lock GET_LOCK('bili_v8_upgrade_<db>'). Two bili processes booting against
the same library can no longer double-delete dup groups or double-refund
CAS refs. The lock is connection-scoped (auto-released if the migrator
dies), scoped per database, and waiters retry until acquired — the

partially undercuts the #4806 streaming fix. Parse the decimal string
explicitly (Number + isFinite guard); the stored value is unchanged, only the

fix: route the fork lane through the network storage backend (#4911)

The MySQL full-mode fork lane never reached the unified backend:
UnifiedShadow's sync facades (lastLiveSeq/cloneSessionRows) return
miss values when sync === null, so MysqlBackend's ready-made twins
had no callers. The fork endpoint is async, so wire it through new
async twins following the established viaAsync pattern:

- shadow: lastLiveSeqAsync / cloneSessionRowsAsync (sqlite delegates
  to the identical sync bodies; mysql routes through the backend on
  the serial queue; a failed/disabled sidecar degrades to the
  kernel-only fork and never fails the fork)
- persist: unifiedLastLiveSeqAsync / unifiedCloneSessionRowsAsync
  replace the now-orphaned sync wrappers
- plugin: handlePluginFork awaits them (the withSessionLock callback
  becomes async; lock scope and ordering are unchanged)
- store/backend: UnifiedStore.cloneSessionRows reports false for an
  absent parent (SqliteBackend no longer resolves an unconditional
  true — matches MysqlBackend semantics)

Same defect family as the V2-lane fix in this PR: a whole-buffer

Found by a full-repo sweep of TextDecoder uses while reviewing this PR.

  probe runs on EVERY POST, proxy up or down — the widest trigger of the

  unknown -> bodyProvablyOverWindow bills ALL bytes as core text
  (media=0), the conservative local-refusal direction, same convention as
  its Request branch returning undefined for unreadable bodies.
- dsh-native.ts rawBodyStringOf: same conservative convention via
  sharedBodyProvablyOverWindow (verbatim copy of the same two lines).
- dsh-native.ts bodyJsonOf (default utf-8 branch): undefined = unreadable,
  exactly like its content-encoding branch already did; every caller
  treats undefined as a clean skip.

Decodable paths are byte-for-byte unchanged (no behavior change for any
body that can be decoded). Tests: route-level pin through the shared
intercept doom arm (throwing decoder + typed-array over-bar body -> clean

RangeError on the pre-fix code) plus both-direction pins that decodable

turn-integrity gate judged the fold over this unit's ids only and withdrew ids

served-markers: graceful dispose records stoppedAt — restart flows no longer raise split-brain alarms (#3923)

A SIGTERM'd proxy's final marker write (dispose flush) lands with a fresh
mtime seconds before its successor rebinds; findContestedWriters' 30s

crashed peers (no stoppedAt), preserving cross-platform pid invisibility
coverage. Two regression tests pin both paths.

makeDispatcher awaited the ENTIRE pipeline (last relayed byte) before

fix: stop draining proxies from claiming their freed port — stale-twin misclassification no longer kills same-lane newcomers (#4982)

A proxy entering graceful shutdown releases its listening socket immediately but kept its registry marker until the drain finished (seconds-to-minutes later). During that window the marker still claimed the port while a different instance could bind it; a same-lane newcomer hitting EADDRINUSE then misclassified the draining predecessor as its twin and died with the adopt signal (exit 3), stranding its launcher behind a cross-lane stranger it is forbidden to attach to (#1225). CI hit this in the #3203 concurrent-sessions e2e (release v0.1.209, run 40574417718).

Two complementary fixes:
- shutdown() stamps portReleasedAt on its own marker the moment the listener closes; classifySameLanePeer skips stamped entries, so a draining instance can never be mistaken for the port holder again (predecessor-wait consumers keep counting them, preserving #3044/#1723).
- the late EADDRINUSE path now verifies the claimed twin's socket ownership via /__bili/health (pid + instance identity, the #4341 criterion) before declaring twin-collision; an unverified claim falls through to the plain foreign-holder policy and ladders.

tests/issue4982-draining-twin-ladder.test.ts pins both halves end to end: a real draining predecessor + silent squatter (newcomer must ladder, not die) and an unstamped marker variant (verification demotes the claim, logged as 'no longer answers as itself').

* fix: reach pages in Firefox-family windows at the default depths (#56)

Firefox and its forks expose a page through their own UI Automation
provider (FrameworkId "Gecko") under three unnamed panes, so the default
tree and snapshot depths stopped one or two levels inside the page and find
missed most of it. In window-scoped trees those panes no longer use up
maxDepth, the same rule Chromium layout panes follow. Measured on Firefox
158, the page tree is present on the first UI Automation call, so no
warm-up is added.

profile and a local page; it skips when no Firefox is installed.
